issues: Meaning drift/terminology: "Mengingat" should be rendered as "Considering" or "Having regard to", not "In View of" (nonstandard legal formula).

Minor meaning drift: "derajad" is "degree" in the text but intended meaning is "human dignity and status/degree of humanity"; current phrasing "human dignity and degree" is awkward and risks misinterpretation.
Punctuation/parenthesis error in item 10: missing closing parenthesis after the Indonesian explanatory title, causing malformed structure.

Meaning drift in item 18: original refers to amendment by Government Regulation No. 58 of 2010 to Government Regulation No. 27 of 1983; translation incorrectly says amendment to Government Regulation No. 90 of 2010 and mismatches year/State Gazette details.
Meaning drift in item 18: the original refers to an amendment to Government Regulation No. 90 of 2010, but the translation changes it to an amendment to Government Regulation No. 27 of 1983.

Minor meaning/terminology drift in item 16: 'Pemberantasan' is better rendered as 'Eradication'/'Combating' rather than 'Eradication of the Criminal Act' (awkward but not fatal); main required fix is the incorrect reference in item 18.
Meaning drift in item 18: Indonesian term 'Pengiriman' means 'Dispatch/Sending', but translation uses 'Transfer', which conflicts with item 7 already covering 'transfer' and changes the defined term.

Minor meaning/wording error in item 11: 'gugurnya pingsan' is rendered as 'miscarriage and fainting' but the structure is awkward; should clearly list consequences (pain, injury/wounds, miscarriage, fainting, and/or death).

Missing end punctuation consistent with list items 31 and 32 (original items end without period, but translation should preserve clear sentence termination; add periods for legal-text clarity without changing structure).
Meaning drift in item 18: 'melabuhkan' means to disembark/land (arrive), not 'landing a person from one place to another' (should be 'to another place').
Minor meaning drift/terminology in item 23: 'Pendamping' is better rendered as 'assistant/advocate' rather than 'Companion' (which can mislead in legal context).
Scrambled/merged list and numbering structure: in Article 3 item e is merged into item d on the same line.

Scrambled/merged list and numbering structure: in Article 9 paragraph (1) sub-items a and b are merged into the same line as the main sentence, and paragraph (2) marker is merged into the end of paragraph (1) instead of appearing as its own numbered item.
Scrambled/merged list structure: in Article 11 items f and i are merged into items e and h respectively (missing line breaks), disrupting list boundaries.

Scrambled/incorrect list structure in Article 3: item e is merged into item d in the original ("...Orang.  e.") but appears as a separate line without preserving the original marker placement; needs to preserve the exact a–e sequence as separate items.

Scrambled/incorrect list structure in Article 11: in the original, items e–i are run together ("...non judgemental)f. ...; ...; dani. Terpadu.") but the translation reformats them; list markers must appear once and in the same order and be correctly associated with their content.
Scrambled numbering/list structure in Article 15: item (2) is merged into item 1.k instead of appearing as a separate numbered item.
Scrambled lettering in Article 21: list item 'e.' is merged into item 'd.' as 'ande.' (should be separate 'e.').
Minor meaning drift in Article 15.k: 'penanganan' translated as 'treatment' (better 'handling/assistance/services') in this legal-service context.

Scrambled numbering/marker structure in Article 15(1): the original has item 1 with sub-items a–k, then continues with “(2) …”; the translation incorrectly makes this a separate top-level item “2.” instead of “(2)” within Article 15.

Meaning drift in Article 15(1): “Tugas Pekerja Sosial sebagai pendamping adalah:a.” is rendered with a line break and indentation that changes the marker association; needs to keep “a.” as part of item (1) exactly as in the original structure.
Scrambled list/numbering in Article 26(2): sub-items a–e are run together ("services for:a.", "ande."), which breaks the required list-marker structure.
Minor meaning/clarity issue in Article 26(2): "dane" in the source corresponds to "and e"; needs separation to preserve the intended enumeration.

Broken/scrambled list structure in Article 26(2): original has inline 'layanan:a.' and 'dane.'; translation reformats into a nested list, which may break downstream marker-based splitting and does not preserve the original marker placement.

Meaning drift in Article 30(2): 'sejak Peraturan Daerah ini ditetapkan' means 'since this Regional Regulation is stipulated/enacted (adopted)', not 'from the enactment' (which can be read as coming into force).
Meaning drift in Article 29: 'diancam dengan hukuman pidana' is 'shall be subject to/threatened with criminal penalties'; 'shall be threatened with criminal punishment' is awkward and can be misread.
